title: CRLR/171/2022 of SUNIL RATURI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
DAILY LOK ADALAT
Criminal Revision No. 171 of 2022
Sunil Raturi ........Revisionist
Versus

State of Uttarakhand and another ........Respondents
Present:

Mr. Pankaj Kumar Sharma, Advocate, for the revisionist.
Mr. Deepak Bhardwaj, learned Brief Holder for the State/respondent no.1.
Mr. Anil Anthwal, Advocate for the respondent no.2.
 Daily Lok Adalat Award
Hon'ble J.C.S. Rawat, J. (Retd.)
Mahesh Chandra Pant, Member/Mediator
 This is a criminal revision by which the revisionist
has prayed to quash the impugned order dated 23.07.2019 passed
by learned Judicial Magistrate/Civil Judge (Jr. Division)
Rishikesh, District Dehradun in Complaint Case No. 49 of 2015
titled as Smt. Maheshwari Devi vs. Sunil Raturi for the offence
punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
The said judgment and order of the learned Magistrate has been
affirmed by the Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun in
Criminal Appeal No. 205 of 2019 whereby the Ist Additional
Sessions Judge, has dismissed the criminal appeal. Now the
matter has been amicably settled by the parties and a settlement
deed has been filed before the Daily Lok Adalat by the private
respondents.

2
2. Both the parties have filed a compromise deed before
the Daily Lok Adalat which runs as under:-
"In the present criminal revision the revisionist has
challenged the order dated 23.07.2019 passed by learned Judicial
Magistrate/Civil Judge (Jr. Division) Rishikesh, in Complaint Case
No. 49 of 2015 "Smt. Maheshwari Devi vs. Sunil Raturi" under
Section 138 of N.I. Act by which the learned court below has
directed the revisionist has convicted and sentence to undergo two
years simple imprisonment and fine of Rs. 16,10,000/- in league
with judgment and order dated 27.08.2021 passed by learned
Additional Sessions Judge Dehradun in Criminal Appeal No. 205 of
2019 "Sunil Raturi vs. Smt. Maheshwari Devi and another."
During pendency of criminal revision before this Hon'ble
Court the parties have reached into amicable settlement and the
revisionist had paid the entire amount of fine i.e. Rs. 16,10,000/- to
the respondent no.2 and on the basis of amicably settlement and on
the basis of amicable settlement the revisionist as well as
respondent no.2 filed compounding application for set aside the
judgment of conviction before this Hon'ble Court and waived off
the fine in the light of judgment rendered in the case of " Madhya
Pradesh State Legal Services Authority vs. Prateek Jain and
another" reported in (2014) SCR 743 as the revisionist was poor
person and was unable to arrange the such amount of fine, hence
the considering facts and circumstances the amount of fine may
kindly be waived off at present there is no dispute survives between
the parties.
 Prayer
 It is therefore, prayed that to set aside the order dated
23.07.2019 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate/Civil Judge

3
(Jr. Division) Rishikesh, in Complaint Case No. 49 of 2015
"Smt. Maheshwari Devi vs. Sunil Raturi" under Section 138 of
N.I. Act in league with judgment and order dated 27.08.2021
passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun in
Criminal Appeal No. 205 of 2019 "Sunil Raturi vs. Smt.
Maheshwari Devi and another" on the basis of the amicable
settlement arrived between the parties and waived off the fine in
the light of judgment rendered in the case of " Madhya Pradesh
State Legal Services Authority vs. Prateek Jain and another"
reported in (2014) SCR 743.
 (Pankaj Kumar Sharma) (Anil Anthwal)
 Counsel for revisionist Counsel for respondent no.2"

3. In view of the above compromise, the judgment and
the conviction order passed by the learned trial courts and the
learned appellate court are liable to be set aside and the
conviction of imprisonment and compensation imposed by the
learned trial court is liable to be set aside and the accused is
liable to be set free from all liabilities.
4. The parties have also filed an application to waive the
penalty imposed upon the accused under Section 138 of
Negotiable Instruments Act on the ground alleged in the
application. They have alleged in the application that the
revisionist is a poor person and as such he was not in a position
to pay the said amount. Apart from that both the parties
contended that the revisionist is a poor person.

4
5. In view of the above the learned counsel for the
parties prayed that the penalty imposed by the under trial court
be waived in terms o f the judgement of the Apex Court in
Madhya Pradesh State Legal Services Authority vs. Prateek Jain
and another, (2014) Volume 10 SCC 690. Thus, in view of the
above, the penalty is waived accordingly in terms of the
compromise.
6. In view of the above the compromise deed the
judgment and orders passed by both the courts below are liable
to be set aside in terms of the compromise.
7. The Revision is disposed of accordingly in terms of
the compromise accordingly. The compromise-deed shall form
part of this award. Let the Trial Court be informed accordingly.
Let a copy of this order be given to both the parties free of cost.
8. All pending applications stand disposed of.
 (Mahesh Chandra Pant, Member) (J.C.S.Rawat, J (Retd.)
 16.10.2024 16.10.2024
Nahid
